subject: Shiny App word-cloud error "Vector size cannot be NA"

messages.author: 1917b9d0b5b9849e
messages.subject: Shiny App word-cloud error "Vector size cannot be NA"
parts:
All,

I downloaded all of the Shiny Apps today and have them working no problem.  I wanted to create my own word cloud ("082-word-cloud") using a text file that when gzip'd is 14.2MB.

When the app starts to work on my file, I see the box pop up that says "Processing Corpus", then after a while it dies with the message "ERROR: vector size cannot be NA"

I have no idea what is causing this. Any help is much appreciated.

Chris.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny App word-cloud error "Vector size cannot be NA"
parts:
Hi Fereshteh,

I literally only changed one line of code in the Word Cloud app.  I changed the line to add a new input from the drop down box.  The changes was in global.R

"
books <<- list("A Mid Summer Night's Dream" = "summer",
              "The Merchant of Venice" = "merchant",
              "Romeo and Juliet" = "romeo",
              "MY NEW DROP DOWN MENU ITEM" = "MYMENUITEM"

Then I have a file called something like MYMENUITEM.txt.gz in the working directory.  Everything works fine, it finds the file, starts processing it, but bombs out.

A couple of things that might help:
  -- my .txt file was built from an Excel CSV export, where I only exported the column I was interested in.  I just changed the file extension from .csv to .txt (perhaps this was the problem?)
  -- when I exported, I exported in Western European ASCII vice UTF-8.  I think I read somewhere that Shiny wanted ASCII
  -- the file has lots of junk in it like slashes, semicolons, parens, etc., etc.  (but I don't think that this is really a problem)

I think the main thing is the error message is not very descriptive.

I have not thought about putting debug statements in there, do you mean something to the effect of print statements like ("here"), etc.?  I haven't tried debugging in R yet.

Thanks!
Chris.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny App word-cloud error "Vector size cannot be NA"
parts:
These are all possibilities. The processing of the file happens in the external packages (tm package) and not by Shiny.
I suggest that you create a very simple text file, and use that as the source for your code change. If that works (I am pretty sure it would), then you know that it is the source file that causes problem. And then you need to narrow down what in the file is causing the problem. If you want you can send your file to us. We can't promise to spend too much time on this, but it might something that we can figure out with a few minutes of time.

Got a little more detail over in the RStudio window tonight:

Warning in nr * nc : NAs produced by integer overflow
Error in vector(typeof(x$v), nr * nc) : vector size cannot be NA

My document has 6.5 million words.  I changed the GUI setting from max words of 300 to 30,000,000.  I thought that was going to help, and it seemed to run longer, but then the same error.
